summary: The Secretary of State is California's chief elections officer, certifying results, maintaining the statewide voter database, and overseeing campaign-finance and business filings. Incumbent Democrat Shirley Weber, appointed in 2021 and elected in 2022 with 60.1%, is seeking a second full term. She placed first in the June 2 primary with 58.70%; Republican Donald P. Wagner, an Orange County supervisor and former assemblymember, placed second with 36.74%.

positions.stance: Says accuracy matters more than speed in California's multi-week count. (CalMatters)
Oversaw permanent universal vote-by-mail and the 2021 recall; platform is expanding voting access, more transparent election filings, and stronger cybersecurity. (CalMatters voter guide)
Has sued local governments over voting rules, including, with Attorney General Bonta, Huntington Beach over its voter-ID measure. (CalMatters; San Joaquin Valley Sun)
Responded to a 2026 U.S. Department of Justice letter about voter rolls by saying her office remains committed to a fair, smooth general election. (Secretary of State press release)
Supports requiring voter ID at the polls. (CalMatters)
Says the slow count undermines public trust and blames Weber for it. (CalMatters)
As county supervisor, pushed for sensitive voter information to be released to the Trump Justice Department over claims of irregularities. (CalMatters voter guide)

key_differences: Voter ID: Wagner wants it at the polls; Weber has sued a city (Huntington Beach) that tried to require it locally.
Federal access to voter rolls: Wagner backed handing voter data to the U.S. Justice Department; Weber's office has resisted.
Speed versus process: both talk about trust, but Wagner frames the multi-week count as the problem while Weber defends it as the cost of accuracy under universal mail voting.
